items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: I told this accountant, Max Tanoff was the attorney and Al Kauf -- Al Tanoff and Max Kaufman. Kaufman was the attorney and Tanoff was the accountant, with Joe Gallo.

ctx.x: Yeah, there was a guy named Johnny Roberts, who was a light hood over from Brooklyn. And he wanted me to record for Brunswick Records. He used to get dates for me. I told him I didn't want to do it because I was -- I had my own company going, and so I told this accountant, Max Tanoff was the attorney and Al Kauf -- Al Tanoff and Max Kaufman. Kaufman was the attorney and Tanoff was the accountant, with Joe Gallo. And I told him, would they speak --

I didn't know Joe Gallo was who he was. I said, 'Will you speak to this guy Johnny Roberts, he wants me to do a date. And he keeps bugging me about it.' And I know he's a gangster, too. I was leery about telling him I didn't want to do it. But he told me not to do anything until our contract was straight with them.
